Deadlines
Deadline
Applies to
December 15
Fall admission opens – strict deadline for PhD and MSI; MA and MSQIST admissions become
rolling from this date
May 1
Fall admission for MA and MSQIST – full-consideration deadline for all applicants,
and final deadline for international applicants
June 15
Fall admission for MA and MSQIST – final deadline for domestic applicants
April 15
Deadline to accept a PhD admission offer
October 1
Spring admission – PhD, MA, MSI; Contact Department
PhD and MSI Fall applications have one strict deadline: December 15.
MA and MSQIST Fall admissions are rolling, opening December 15. International applicants
must apply by May 1, which is also the deadline for full consideration. Domestic applicants
have until June 15 to apply, but should also aim for May 1 to receive full consideration.
Spring admission is very limited, and it is practically impossible to secure a teaching-assistant
position for a Spring start. Please contact the department before applying for Spring Admission in any degree program. Applications from prospective MA and MSI students for Spring are welcome; PhD applicants
should only apply for Spring admission if they already have a pre-arranged source
of funding.
If you are applying to the PhD or MSI program from a country where your local deadlines
run later than ours (for example, much of Europe) and you missed our December 15 deadline,
contact the Graduate Program Director. If we still have open positions, late applications
are considered until June 15, though the admission rate for these is much lower than
for applications received by the regular deadline.
Eligibility and Requirements
The Graduate School requires a minimum GPA of 3.0 for admission to any graduate program
at Stony Brook. If your GPA is below 3.0, admission is only possible under exceptional
circumstances, and in most cases you should not apply.
For admission to the PhD, MA, or MSI programs, in addition to the Graduate School’s
requirements, you need:
A bachelor’s degree in physics or a closely related field from an accredited institution.
A minimum grade average of B in all undergraduate coursework, and B or better in your
science and mathematics courses.
In special cases, a student not meeting these two requirements may be admitted on
a provisional basis; if so, you’ll be told what’s needed to end provisional status.
Successful PhD applicants typically have a GPA of at least 3.6 on a 4.0 scale – keep this in mind when deciding whether to apply. The Admissions
Committee reviews each transcript individually, so a lower overall GPA may still receive
serious consideration if your science and math grades are strong.
We do not require the general or Physics GRE for any of our programs, and no longer
accept these scores.
Admission to the MSQIST degree has its own, separate requirements:
An undergraduate degree in science or engineering.
A 100-level, calculus-based introductory physics sequence.
A 200-level Modern Physics course or equivalent. However, most successful applicants
and students will have taken a 300-level undergraduate course in Quantum Physics.
Applying to the MA Program and the PhD Program
If you apply to the PhD program, the application itself lets you indicate that you’d
like to be considered for our MA program in case you are not admitted to the PhD program
– no second application is required. Indicating this interest will not reduce your chances of PhD admission. Note that if you already hold a Master’s degree
in Physics, we cannot admit you to our MA program.
English Language Requirements
Applicants who are not native or primary speakers of English, and don’t otherwise
qualify for an exemption (e.g. a degree from an English-instruction institution, US
citizenship/National status, or English-instruction TA experience), must submit TOEFL,
IELTS, or Gateway English Test scores. Under the TOEFL iBT’s current scoring scale
(effective January 21, 2026), the minimum overall score is 5 for doctoral applicants and 4.5 for master’s applicants.
A separate, higher speaking-score threshold determines Teaching Assistant eligibility.
Applicants who don’t meet it may still be admitted but will not be allowed to serve
as a TA until they complete a sequence of remedial Oral Academic English (OAE) courses.
All applicants must declare their native language as part of the admission process;
intentional misrepresentation is academic dishonesty and grounds for dismissal. TOEFL
and IELTS scores cannot be more than 2 years old. Have ETS send your TOEFL scores
directly to the Graduate School (institution code 2548) – paper copies are not accepted.
See the Graduate Catalog’s English Language Proficiency policy for the full score tables (TOEFL, IELTS, Gateway, and the TA speaking-score breakdown),
complete exemption criteria, and conditional-admission details.
How to Apply
All applications are submitted online at the Graduate Admissions page. Before starting, read the “Application Instructions” linked from that page. You
can only access the full application once the application fee is paid.
Your application should include:
A statement of purpose, describing your interests and motivation for pursuing a PhD or MA/MSI degree. It
will be read by physicists outside your specific field, so keep it at a level any
physics bachelor’s graduate can follow, and keep it to 1-2 pages – we read hundreds
of these, and a concise, exciting statement stands out. Mention faculty you’d like
to work with (no need to contact them in advance). In the current system, the statement
of purpose and CV are uploaded as additional materials after the rest of your application.
Transcripts from every college and university you’ve attended, uploaded electronically, along
with your CV. Only applications with an uploaded transcript will be considered; we’ll
request two official paper copies only after you’re admitted.
Three letters of recommendation, submitted electronically.
TOEFL/IELTS scores, if required – see English Language Requirements above.
If you’re applying before your Fall grades are available, send your transcript without
them by the deadline; you can send an updated transcript later, though there’s no
guarantee it will be used in the decision. If admitted, you’ll eventually need to
submit a complete official transcript with all grades.
Application Fee and Fee Waivers
An application fee of $100 is required. Domestic (US) applicants may be eligible for
a waiver – see the eligibility requirements and waiver procedure from the Graduate School. If you’re not eligible, we regret that we’re not able to
waive the application fee.
Funding and Tuition
PhD students receive full financial support for the duration of their studies. Most
are supported as a Teaching Assistant (TA) or Research Assistant (RA); some may also
have grants, scholarships, or fellowships. The current 9-month TA stipend is $30,000,
plus an additional $8,000 for a full summer TA position. Research Assistant salaries
are:

Research Assitant Salary
2026
$41,000
2027

The TA stipend is expected to rise over this same period to match the RA salary schedule.
PhD students also receive a scholarship covering full tuition and most fees. See The
PhD page’s Graduate Funding section – particularly Tuition – for the full policy details.
MSI students typically receive a tuition waiver for the duration of their studies;
a stipend is not guaranteed beyond that, though many find support through a Teaching
Assistant appointment – see Funding and Tuition on the MSI page for details.
MA and MSQIST students are not guaranteed financial support, though they may find
support from a research group. Students hired as an RA or TA do not receive a tuition
scholarship; tuition cost depends on residency status – see the Cost of Attendance page for current figures.
After You Apply
PhD and MSI admission decisions are only made after the December 15 deadline. The
bulk of our offers go out in February and March, and most applicants hear from us
well before April 1. MA and MSQIST applications are reviewed, and decisions made,
on a rolling basis as they arrive.
All applications are evaluated centrally by the Admissions Committee – there’s no
need to contact individual faculty, though you should mention in your application
which faculty you’d be interested in working with.
You’re welcome to visit the department any time, and we’re happy to help plan your
trip. Once admitted, limited travel-reimbursement support is available (US citizens/permanent
residents only). The best time to visit is our “visiting weekend,” usually a Sunday-Monday
in March.
Accepting Your Offer
PhD offers must be accepted online by April 15, a date agreed upon by the Council of Graduate Schools’ April 15 Resolution. This agreement was recently reaffirmed, and most schools honor this date. Any doctoral
program pressuring you to decide earlier than April 15 is profoundly disrespectful
of your decision process. Offers for other graduate degrees (i.e. not funded doctoral
programs), may have different acceptance dates specified in the offer letter. If you
miss your deadline, your spot may be offered to another student. If you’re declining
an offer, please do so as soon as possible so we can offer the spot to someone else.
If our offer expires without a response by April 15, we assume it’s been declined.
In some years we may have positions open after the deadline – if you’d like to be
reconsidered, contact the Graduate Program Director.
